doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Army service as a radio operator
summary: A classification specialist made him a high-speed radio operator at Southeast Signal School for two years during the Korean War, thanks to his radio jingle job.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. What did you do in the service?

I was a radio operator. I was fortunate to have, they called them Classification Specialists, who would interview you, as you are interviewing me, and determine how I would best serve Uncle Sam. It was the time of the Korean War and so you would think that they would exercise a little more wisdom than they did in my case. Well I’ll give you an example. This Classification Specialist sits me down and says, “What did you do in civilian life?” I said, “Well I just graduated from Hamilton College. I had a job with Batton, Barton, Durston and Osborne, it’s an advertising agency.” And he says, “Well we don’t need advertising in the Army. What did you actually do?” I said, “Well I wrote radio jingles, ‘tune in tonight and hear Jack Benny and Phil Harris and all that.’” “Radio? You’re a radio man.” Dede det de det. Off I went to the Southeast Signal School and for two years I was a high speed radio operator.
You said the magic word for him I guess.
Yeah. Radio was it. “He’s a radioman.”
